macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds toward $64,000 after Coldcard exploit and Strategy sales
items.summary: Bitcoin rose about 1.6% in the last 24 hours to around $63,692, after briefly reaching $64,160, as markets absorbed fallout from a Coldcard wallet exploit and recent bitcoin sales by Strategy. CoinDesk said roughly 1,816 BTC, worth about $114 million, were removed from more than 5,200 addresses, while the Crypto Fear & Greed Index fell to 'extreme fear'.

items.title: Crypto market braces after Coldcard hack tops $100 million in losses
items.summary: CryptoRank reported confirmed losses above $100 million from a Coldcard hack, including 1,596 BTC stolen, underscoring ongoing wallet-custody security risks. The same recap said Bitcoin traded near $63,824, total crypto market cap reached $2.18 trillion, and 24-hour liquidations climbed to $224.06 million.

items.title: Crypto prices mixed as geopolitical tension keeps traders cautious
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reported Bitcoin around $63,470, Ethereum near $1,853, XRP at about $1.07, and Solana near $73.11 over the last 24 hours, with over $240 million liquidated across the market. The article said traders were weighing geopolitical risk from Iran against selling pressure from large corporate bitcoin holders.

items.title: Senate crypto bill debate centers on blockchain developer protections
items.summary: The Block reported that Senator Wyden urged Senate leaders to preserve contested blockchain developer protections in the broader crypto bill. The same coverage also noted pressure around the U.S. CLARITY Act and related legislative deadlines shaping the regulatory agenda.

items.title: White House silence leaves CLARITY Act stalled, according to market recap
items.summary: CryptoRank said the CLARITY Act remains stalled because the White House has not responded to an ethics compromise. That report framed the delay as one of the key regulatory overhangs for the crypto market over the past 24 hours.

items.title: Binance Wallet adds Plume yield vaults tied to Invesco and Bitwise funds
items.summary: The Block reported that Binance Wallet added Plume's yield vault offering, giving users access to products linked to Invesco and Bitwise funds. The move highlights continued growth in tokenized and yield-oriented crypto products.

items.title: BNB Chain announces new Layer 1 for agentic trading
items.summary: The Block said BNB Chain is building a new Layer 1 focused on agentic trading, with a target mainnet launch in 2027. The project is a notable infrastructure development aimed at automation-heavy crypto market activity.

items.title: Cardano governance role changes after wallet exploit
items.summary: The Block reported that EMURGO, Cardano's founding entity, stepped down from its Pentad governance role following a wallet exploit. The change reflects continuing security and governance repercussions in major blockchain ecosystems.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across different applications and files, intensifying competition in professional AI tools. The launch signals a continued push toward agentic software that can perform end-to-end work tasks.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-Live voice models
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The release adds to the rapid expansion of multimodal AI capabilities.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to its Muse Spark AI model and an upgraded 1.1 version. The move positions Meta more directly against Anthropic and OpenAI in monetizing model access.

items.title: SpaceXAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: SpaceXAI announced Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model yet and optimized for coding and agentic workflows. The launch highlights growing focus on models built for autonomous task execution.

items.title: Anthropic appoints Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic said it appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body charged with keeping the company aligned with its public mission. The move underscores continued governance scrutiny around frontier AI companies.

items.title: New York Times-led publishers ask court to sanction OpenAI
items.summary: A group of newspapers led by The New York Times asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI in an ongoing copyright dispute. The filing escalates legal pressure over allegations that OpenAI misused copyrighted journalism in training.

items.title: Italy fines Character.AI owner for data protection breaches
items.summary: Italy's data protection authority fined Character Technologies, the company behind Character.AI, €158,000 for breaches of data protection rules. The action reflects increasing regulatory scrutiny of consumer AI chatbots and their handling of personal data.

items.title: Meta plans major data center build in central Alberta
items.summary: Meta announced it will build a large data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada. The investment reflects the industry-wide race to expand compute infrastructure for AI training and deployment.

items.title: Anthropic's latest Claude versions lifted from U.S. restrictions
items.summary: AP reported that the Trump administration lifted restrictions on Anthropic's latest Claude versions after a weekslong ban tied to cybersecurity concerns. The decision suggests ongoing policy tension between AI deployment and national-security review.
